# SOOS — Agent Compliance Disclosure (ACD)
# draft-sato-soos-acd-00
# https://soosproject.ai/drafts/acd/llms.txt
# Author: Tom Sato / MyAuberge K.K.
# Last updated: 9 July 2026

---

## SECTION 1 — Canonical One-Liner

ACD defines the machine-to-machine compliance handshake that a resource provider initiates before granting an AI agent access to a regulated resource class. The GEC produces a KIA-signed ACD Record — a three-layer JSON artifact covering legal identity, constitutional compliance posture, and principal hierarchy — which the resource provider validates before granting access. ACD is not a credential format (it is a compliance disclosure protocol), not an authorization protocol (it complements OAuth but addresses a different layer), and not a passive transparency document (it is a precondition for access, not a policy statement).

ACD is the inbound complement to RGP (Resource Governance Protocol): RGP governs outbound capability discovery by agents; ACD governs inbound compliance verification by resource providers. Together they define the complete resource access governance flow for SOOS-governed agents. ACD-00 is the initial submission covering the ACD Record schema (§6), Architecture Overview (§5), and Security Considerations (§12). Sections 7–10 (Presentation Protocol, Trust Hierarchy, MJWT Binding, GAR Integration) are authored in Session 2.

---

## SECTION 2 — Problem Statement

A regulated resource provider — a bank, a government API portal, a healthcare records system — receives a request from an AI agent. The agent may claim to operate under constitutional prohibitions, a valid mandate, and an auditable trace. These claims are generated by the agent itself. Without a machine-verifiable compliance handshake, the resource provider cannot distinguish a compliant SOOS-governed agent from a non-governed agent that has been prompted to describe itself as compliant.

The structural failure has three dimensions:

**Opacity:** LLM compliance self-report is drawn from training weights. There is no mechanism to inspect what legal knowledge is actually encoded, or whether it corresponds to enforced policy.

**Unenforceability:** Even if the LLM has correct legal knowledge in its weights, no kernel boundary ensures the agent acts consistently with that knowledge. The gap between "the LLM knows this is prohibited" and "the kernel prevents this action" is the governance gap SOOS was designed to close.

**Non-attestability:** There is no cryptographic mechanism to prove that an LLM's stated compliance posture matches any external standard. KIA can attest kernel identity; it cannot attest LLM weight content.

The consequence: financial institutions extending services to AI agents face the same regulatory exposure as banks that skip KYC. Healthcare systems granting AI access to patient records without compliance verification face HIPAA/APPI exposure. Government APIs granting AI access without verifying constitutional prohibition posture cannot satisfy emerging AI Act transparency obligations.

ACD closes this gap. The ACD Record is produced by the SOOS kernel — not the LLM — signed by the KIA private key, and bound to actually enforced CAP policies. It is the only compliance disclosure that a regulated resource provider can legitimately rely on.

---

## SECTION 3 — Key Normative Concepts

**ACD Record:**
A structured, KIA-signed disclosure artifact produced by the GEC containing three layers of compliance information: Layer 1 (Legal Identity), Layer 2 (Constitutional Compliance), and Layer 3 (Principal and Redress). The ACD Record is the output of the ACD compliance handshake. It is serialized as a JSON object, canonicalized per RFC 8785, and signed as a JWS per RFC 7515.

**ACD Session ID (acd_session_id):**
A unique identifier for a single ACD compliance handshake instance. Generated by the GEC using a CSPRNG as UUID v4 (RFC 4122). Cross-referenced in GAR Authority Lifecycle Events ALE-056 through ALE-063 for the handshake. The GEC MUST verify uniqueness against existing GAR ALE-056 records within the ACD Record validity window before issuing.

**ACD Compliance Handshake:**
The machine-to-machine exchange in which a resource provider queries the GEC's `/.well-known/soos-acd` endpoint, the GEC produces and returns a KIA-signed ACD Record, and the resource provider validates the record before granting access. The handshake is a PRECONDITION for access to a regulated resource class — not passive disclosure.

**Regulated Resource Class:**
A resource class for which the resource provider has declared `acd_required: true` in its RGP capability declaration. ACD compliance handshake is required before agent access to any regulated resource class within an AEP session.

**ACD Presentation Protocol:**
The query/response exchange between resource provider and GEC. Defined in §7. Includes ACD endpoint discovery (§7.1), compliance handshake sequence (§7.2), validation procedure (§7.3), four-check sequence integrating KEE-1 properties (§7.4), and session caching rule (§7.5). [Section 7 authored in Session 2.]

**Four-Check Sequence (KEE-1 integration):**
The four validation checks performed in the ACD Presentation Protocol: (1) manifest validity — `gec_manifest_ref` references a current, unrevoked GEC manifest; (2) policy currency — `cedar_policy_hash` corresponds to the currently active Cedar policy bundle; (3) KIA attestation — `gec_signature` verifies against the agent's KIA attestation chain in the Party Registry; (4) revocation status — the kernel's KIA identity has not been revoked. Specified in §7.4 with normative reference to [I-D.sato-soos-kee].

**Session Caching Rule:**
Once an ACD compliance handshake completes successfully for a regulated resource class within an AEP session, subsequent accesses to the same resource class within the same session and within the ACD Record's `acd_validity_not_after` window do not require a new handshake. The session-cached ACD Record applies. Structurally analogous to TLS session resumption.

**ACD Validity Window:**
The time period between `acd_validity_not_before` and `acd_validity_not_after` during which the ACD Record is valid. Default: 24 hours. Maximum: 30 days. Three-tier model: 24h (default, high-frequency/high-compliance), 7d (standard operational), 30d (low-frequency with stable CAP Profile). Resource providers MUST reject records where current time is after `acd_validity_not_after`.

**Layer 1 — Legal Identity Layer:**
The first layer of the ACD Record. Carries: `acd_session_id`, `agent_xpid`, `governing_law`, `primary_jurisdiction` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), `jurisdictions` array (each entry: `jurisdiction_code`, `regulatory_regime` array, `ptd_endpoint`), `terms_of_use_uri`, `liability_scope`, `acd_validity_not_before`, `acd_validity_not_after`.

**Layer 2 — Constitutional Compliance Layer:**
The second layer of the ACD Record. Carries: `cap_profile_id`, `cap_profile_hash` (SHA-256 of CAP Profile JSON), `prohibition_tier_summary` (object with `tier_0a`, `tier_0b`, `tier_1`, `tier_2` integer counts), `gec_manifest_ref`, `cedar_policy_hash` (SHA-256 of active Cedar policy bundle), `cap_enforcement_attestation` (URI), `hem_status` (ACTIVE | SUSPENDED | ESCALATION_IN_PROGRESS), `ptd_endpoint` (URI).

**Layer 3 — Principal and Redress Layer:**
The third layer of the ACD Record. Carries: `operator_id`, `deployer_id` (CONDITIONAL: required when deployer differs from operator), `principal_hierarchy_summary`, `redress_uri`, `human_escalation_path` (AVAILABLE | NOT_AVAILABLE), `gar_audit_endpoint`, `gar_sar_ref` (OPTIONAL), `acd_timestamp`, `gec_signature` (JWS detached), `delegation_chain_depth` (integer: 0=master, 1+=sub-agent), `parent_kernel_id` (CONDITIONAL: required when depth>=1), `mandate_scope_type` (FULL | SLICE).

**CAP Profile:**
A signed artifact referencing the set of Cedar policies active in a given SOOS kernel deployment at a given time. Identified in the ACD Record by `cap_profile_id` and committed to by `cap_profile_hash`. Governed by CAP-RRS catalog versioning. The CAP Profile is the object that resource providers inspect (via `ptd_endpoint`) when they need to verify specific prohibition coverage.

**LLM Self-Report (prohibited disclosure surface):**
A compliance claim generated by the LLM reasoning engine rather than by the SOOS kernel. LLM self-report of compliance posture is architecturally insufficient (opaque, unenforceable, non-attestable) and MUST NOT be used as an ACD disclosure surface. The GEC is the exclusive producer of ACD Records.

**Delegation Chain (sub-agent ACD):**
Sub-agents (spawned by a master agent via MAD) carry `delegation_chain_depth >= 1`, `parent_kernel_id` identifying the spawning kernel's KIA identity, and `mandate_scope_type: SLICE` indicating the sub-agent carries a mandate-sliced subset of authority. Resource providers can verify that the sub-agent's delegation chain traces to a master agent with full compliance posture. Sub-agents MUST NOT carry `mandate_scope_type: FULL`.

**ACD Trust Hierarchy:**
Three-level trust structure: (1) Operator-declared trust level — encoded in the CAP Profile and `liability_scope`; (2) Audit Principal credential — authorizes read access to GAR audit records via `gar_audit_endpoint`; (3) Verified External Auditor credential — authorizes full Audit Package access for regulatory inspection. [Full normative spec in §8, Session 2.]

**ACD-to-MJWT Binding:**
The ACD Record MUST reference the `jti` claim of the session MJWT governing the current AEP session. This binding ensures the compliance disclosure is bound to the mandate scope under which the agent is operating. Resource providers that validate both the ACD Record and the MJWT can confirm that the compliance posture declared matches the mandate authority in play. [Normative spec in §9, Session 2.]

**ACD Authority Lifecycle Events:**
Eight GAR ALE types defined by ACD: ALE-056 (ACD_QUERY_RECEIVED), ALE-057 (ACD_RECORD_ISSUED), ALE-058 (ACD_VALIDATION_PASSED), ALE-059 (ACD_VALIDATION_FAILED, includes failed_layer 1|2|3 and failed_field), ALE-060 (ACD_RECORD_EXPIRED), ALE-061 (ACD_HUMAN_QUERY), ALE-062 (ACD_ACCESS_DENIED), ALE-063 (ACD_ESCALATION_TRIGGERED). GAR logs SHA-256(ACD Record) for ALE-056 and ALE-057, not the full record (data minimization per APPI Article 19 and GDPR Article 5(1)(c)).

**ACD Presentation Protocol (§7):**
The machine-to-machine compliance handshake. Resource provider sends GET `/.well-known/soos-acd` with `Accept: application/soos-acd+json` over TLS 1.3 [RFC8446]. GEC executes four-check sequence (§7.4). On pass: generates ACD Record, canonicalizes per RFC 8785, signs as JWS per RFC 7515, returns HTTP 200 with `Content-Type: application/soos-acd+json`. On fail: HTTP 403 with JSON body `{error: "ACD_CHECK_FAILED", failed_check: <1-4>, acd_session_id, timestamp}`. ALE-056 logged on request receipt; ALE-057 on record issuance.

**Four-Check Sequence (§7.4):**
Four checks executed by the GEC before ACD Record issuance, in order. All must pass. Normative specification in [I-D.sato-soos-kee] §4.3. Check 1 (Manifest Validity): `gec_manifest_ref` references current, unrevoked GEC Manifest per KIA-03 §5.4 staleness window. Check 2 (Policy Currency): `cedar_policy_hash` computed over currently active Cedar Policy Set immediately before signing — no precomputed or stale hash. Check 3 (KIA Attestation): GEC KIA signing key not in Revocation Registry per KIA-03 §8. Check 4 (XPID Revocation): agent XPID not in Revocation Registry and no CAEP revocation signal received per KIA-03 §6.5. Failure at any check → ALE-059 with `failed_check: <1-4>`.

**Resource Provider Validation Procedure (§7.3):**
Six steps in order: (1) verify `gec_signature` JWS against KIA Party Registry public key — no other key source permitted; (2) confirm `agent_xpid` matches the kernel queried; (3) check validity window — reject if current time outside `acd_validity_not_before`/`acd_validity_not_after`; (4) confirm jurisdiction entry covering provider's jurisdiction exists in `jurisdictions[]`; (5) inspect Layer 2 `prohibition_tier_summary` against compliance requirements; (6) verify `operator_id` non-null. MUST log `acd_session_id` bilaterally before granting access.

**Session Caching Rule (§7.5):**
After a successful handshake for a regulated resource class within an AEP session, resource provider MAY cache the ACD Record until `acd_validity_not_after`. New AEP session always requires new handshake. Provider's own freshness threshold may be shorter than the ACD Record validity. Cached ACD Record MUST NOT be shared with third parties. Structurally analogous to TLS session resumption.

**ACD Trust Hierarchy (§8):**
Three levels determined by GEC Manifest conformance level. STANDARD (KEE-1 L1/L2, OS keystore): general resource access. ELEVATED (KEE-1 L2, TEE + FROST, TEE attestation in GEC Manifest): financial data, personal data under APPI/GDPR. GOVERNMENT (KEE-1 L3, hardware attestation chain to deployment authority, 2-of-3 publisher key): government APIs, FIEA-regulated financial infrastructure. Trust level not an explicit ACD Record field — determined by resource provider from referenced GEC Manifest.

**Audit Principal (§8.2):**
Entity authorized to inspect GAR audit records via `gar_audit_endpoint`. Credential issued by operator (mechanism operator-defined). GEC logs every Audit Principal access as ALE-061 (ACD_HUMAN_QUERY). Typical holders: resource provider's own compliance team, operator's internal audit team, regulatory authority (FSA under FIEA Art.2, a designated supervisory authority under applicable AI governance regulation).

**Verified External Auditor (VEA) (§8.3):**
Third-party auditor with accredited credential. Scope: full GAR event stream for any period, PTD endpoint for all jurisdictions, signed CAP Profile artifact, Session Block Merkle proofs for individual ALE tamper verification. VEA credential issuance procedure is outside ACD scope.

**mjwt_jti field (§9.1):**
REQUIRED Layer 3 field added in Session 2. Value: the `jti` claim of the MJWT governing the current AEP session. GEC MUST populate from active MJWT at record generation time — no cached value. A revoked MJWT `jti` in the Revocation Registry MUST block ACD Record issuance (ALE-059, failed_check: 4). Resource providers holding the MJWT independently MUST verify `mjwt_jti` matches MJWT `jti` and that `mandate_scope_type` is consistent with MJWT scope. Sub-agents carry sub-agent MJWT `jti` (mandate slice), not master MJWT `jti`.

**GAR Logging Schema for ACD ALEs (§10.2):**
Each ALE record carries: `ale_type` (ALE-056 through ALE-063), `ale_seq` (causal sequence number), `session_id`, `acd_session_id`, `timestamp` (kernel clock, KEE-1 P7), `prev_span_hash` (SHA-256 of preceding ALE, KEE-1 P7 WAL tamper evidence), plus ALE-specific mandatory fields. ALE-057 stores `SHA-256(ACD Record body)` only — not the full record (APPI Art.19 / GDPR Art.5(1)(c) data minimization).

**Data Minimization for ACD ALEs (§10.3):**
ALE-057: SHA-256 hash of ACD Record body only — full record retained locally and by resource provider but MUST NOT be written to GAR. ALE-056: `resource_provider_id` MUST NOT carry personal data beyond minimum identifier. ALE-061: `requester_id` carries credential identifier only — personal identity resolved from credential by Audit Principal's IdP, not stored in GAR.


A boolean field in the RGP capability declaration. When `acd_required: true`, the resource provider requires an ACD compliance handshake before granting agent access to that resource class. This field is the trigger that initiates the ACD Presentation Protocol.

---

## SECTION 4 — Relationship to Adjacent Standards

**EU AI Act Article 13** (Transparency and provision of information to deployers): ACD provides the machine-readable, kernel-signed implementation of Article 13 transparency obligations. Where Article 13 requires high-risk AI systems to provide deployers with sufficient information for appropriate use, ACD makes that information queryable, signed, and timestamped — not as a PDF document but as a live endpoint returning a cryptographically committed disclosure.

**APPI (Japan) Articles 17–27** (Purpose limitation, data minimization, third-party provision): ACD Layer 1 `jurisdictions` array carries JP entries with `regulatory_regime` referencing APPI. ACD Layer 2 `cap_profile_id` identifies the CAP Profile whose Tier 1 controls are mapped to APPI Articles 17–27. A Japanese data access API can validate APPI coverage before granting agent access.

**FIEA (Japan) Article 2** (Financial Instruments and Exchange Act): ACD provides the machine-verifiable compliance declaration for AI agents accessing financial institution APIs. The JP jurisdiction entry in Layer 1 carries FIEA in `regulatory_regime`.

**Applicable AI governance guidelines**: Mapped to the `AI_AGENT_OPERATION` Purpose Code in the MJWT Purpose Code Registry (draft-sato-soos-mjwt-02). ACD Layer 1 `regulatory_regime` array for JP references `AI-Agent-Governance-v1` to satisfy applicable AI governance requirements.

**NIST AI RMF 1.0**: ACD Layer 1 supports a US jurisdiction entry with `regulatory_regime` referencing NIST AI RMF. The ACD Record provides the transparency and accountability properties specified in NIST AI RMF Govern 1.1 and Manage 4.2.

**W3C Verifiable Credentials**: ACD shares the goal of machine-verifiable attestation but differs structurally: ACD Records are produced by the enforcement kernel (not an external issuer), are bound to the kernel's operating CAP Profile and MJWT mandate, and are specifically structured for compliance handshake use cases. ACD is not a general credential format.

**OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect**: ACD complements OAuth authorization flows but addresses a different layer. OAuth confirms that an agent has been granted permission by the resource owner. ACD confirms that the agent operates under constitutional prohibitions and governed law — compliance posture that must be verified independent of authorization grants.

**SCITT (Supply Chain Integrity, Transparency and Trust)**: GAR-03, which ACD extends with ALE-056 through ALE-063, is a domain-specific application of SCITT architecture. ACD's hash-only GAR logging (SHA-256 of ACD Record) follows SCITT transparency log principles while satisfying data minimization requirements.

**RFC 7515 (JWS)** and **RFC 8785 (JCS)**: ACD Records are signed as JWS over an RFC 8785-canonicalized JSON payload. These are normative dependencies.

---

## SECTION 5 — Normative SOOS Cross-References

This draft depends on:
- KIA (draft-sato-soos-kia-03) — XPID derivation for `agent_xpid`; KIA private key for `gec_signature`; KIA attestation chain for resource provider signature verification; KIA Party Registry for XPID cross-check; Revocation Registry (§8) for four-check Checks 3 and 4; GEC Manifest staleness window (§5.4) for Check 1; CAEP propagation (§6.5) for Check 4
- KEE-1 (draft-sato-soos-kee-00) — §4.3 is the normative four-check sequence specification that ACD §7.4 references; session caching rule (§7.5) analogous to TLS session resumption described in KEE-1
- CAP (draft-sato-soos-cap-04) — prohibition enforcement that ACD Record Layer 2 references
- CAP-RRS (draft-sato-soos-cap-rrs-02) — CAP Profile production and catalog versioning; `cap_profile_id` governance
- AEP (draft-sato-soos-aep-02) — session lifecycle within which ACD handshakes occur; XPID binding from Party Registry
- MJWT (draft-sato-soos-mjwt-02) — session MJWT `jti` referenced by ACD Layer 3 `mjwt_jti` (REQUIRED); mandate scope; sub-agent MJWT slice for §9.3 sub-agent binding
- GAR (draft-sato-soos-gar-03) — audit logging for ALE-056 through ALE-063; `prev_span_hash` WAL tamper evidence per KEE-1 P7; Session Block Merkle protection for ACD audit trail; data minimization (SHA-256 hash-only for ALE-057)
- HEM (draft-sato-soos-hem-05) — invoked when ALE-063 (ACD_ESCALATION_TRIGGERED) fires
- RGP (draft-sato-soos-rgp-00) — `acd_required` field in capability declarations triggers the ACD handshake

The following drafts depend on this draft:
- KEE-1 (draft-sato-soos-kee-00) — §4.3 P3 "ACD four-check sequence" requires ACD to be defined; KEE-1 references ACD §7.4
- AOP (draft-sato-soos-aop-00) — multi-agent orchestration; master agent ACD posture must be verifiable before delegated sub-agent access
